lines: Dusk over Hollowmere. The lamps going up, one by one, like the city buttoning its coat.
She puts the kettle on when the lamps go up. I am punctual. She is predictable. The arrangement works.
Tonight calls for a gift. A vole, ideally. Voles say what flowers cannot.

scenes.art_desc: Ash pressed low on rooftop tiles, stalking an unaware vole near a chimney pot, warm dusk light
lines: There. Under the chimney pot. Fat, smug, unaware.
Tonight the world is simple, and the world is RED: ferocity, the oldest energy there is.
And one good idea: POUNCE.

coach.text: Where you are. Places have rules; rooftops mostly have wind.
The opposition. Tonight: one vole of tremendous conviction.
Its life is a red thread. Claws do the unstitching.
It telegraphs its next move here. Honesty is its one virtue.
The chronicle. What just happened, one line at a time.
The heart: your lives-worth of tonight. Guard it.
The shield: GUARD soaks a hit, then fades at turn's end.
The spool: energy still wound in your deck. Spent stays spent.
Paws are actions. Placing an energy anywhere spends one.
Your hand is ENERGY — tonight, all Ferocity.
Tap POUNCE.
Feed it Ferocity until every pip is crossed. A full card is a willing card — tap USE.
A breath left in it. SCRATCH — free, once a turn. Finish politely.

lines: Acquired. Thoughtfully dead.
The thrill of a clean hunt sings in every muscle — the whole deck of me, wound fresh.
She will say 'not on the table', and mean 'thank you'.
The vole declines to be a gift tonight.
Dignity intact. Mostly. She will have to make do with my company, which is worth several voles.

scenes.art_desc: The Shambles at night: market stalls sleeping under canvas, crooked timber shopfronts, one lit lantern
lines: Below: the Shambles. By day the whole city trades here — fish, buttons, gossip, gossip about fish.
By night, other markets open. I don't shop there. Often.
Eight bells from the tower. There is no ninth bell. There used to be.

scenes.art_desc: The Shambles at night: market stalls sleeping under canvas, crooked timber shopfronts, one lit lantern
lines: Between the chimneys: a thread of silver light, thin as a hair, humming.
Not mine. Not hers.
I did not chase it. I am a professional.
Street level. The fog rolls up from the Mere, and the shadows deepen — deep enough to wear.
New tonight: SHADOW. Spend it to be somewhere else, quietly.
Ahead, something small and hungry rises from the gutter: a GUTTER-WISP.
Bottle-sized. It eats small lies — and covets shiny things.
It has noticed the vole.

coach.text: Every fight opens with the going-in. STALK it — spend Shadow to begin unseen.
SHADOW, the black energy. Ferocity is the claw; Shadow is the fog — it hides and wards.
Its next move shows up top. 'Steals a card' means your HAND is the target.
SLINK blocks 3 — and Shadow is cheaper in this fog. Try it when a bite is coming.
When your paws are spent, END TURN. The night moves too.

lines: The wisp reconsidered its position on voles.
Something is wrong tonight, and it is not the wisp. No pigeons. Pigeons are never quiet; quiet is against their religion.
I let it keep its opinions. The night is too strange to argue with weather made of appetite.
No pigeons anywhere. Pigeons are never quiet; quiet is against their religion.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit wrong — and the Lamplighters never miss.
Third lesson, then: GUILE, the green energy of patience and timing.
And the deepest defense a cat knows: the LOAF. All paws in. Immovable.
The dog at Number Twelve is awake. Of course it is.

coach.text: Its LUNGE hits for 4. Block BEFORE it lands — or bank a card now and go big later.
LOAF: Block 6, but all paws are committed — you can't act next turn. Time it.

lines: The dog and I have agreed to disagree.
Her window is ahead now. Dark. Her window is never dark.
Last of the four: MYSTICISM. Hers. It becomes whatever the moment needs.
Rare, and rarer to spend well. With it, the oldest medicine: the PURR.
Four is all a cat carries. The claws stay home — you cannot scratch an absence.

coach.text: A RAG-WRAITH: clothes whose owner is missing. Not dead — missing. It is above your weight.
PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — but breaks if you're hit. Purr behind a block.
You do not have to win this. SLIP AWAY costs nothing but pride — and gets you home.

lines: Two ways home from here.
The long way passes the Lamplighters' hall — whatever silenced the lamps went wrong there first.
The fast way is over the fences. Now. While the kettle still screams.
choices: The long way — see what silenced the lamps

scenes.art_desc: Lamplighters' guild hall interior, abandoned mid-shift: racked ladders, cold kettle, one silver thread glinting on a lamp-hook
lines: The Lamplighters' hall: door open, ladders racked, kettle cold. Nobody.
Caught on a lamp-hook: a thread of silver. HER stitching. She was here tonight. Why was she HERE?
I take the thread. It hums against my teeth like a struck bell.
(Her Stitching joins your deck — Mysticism 2.)

scenes.art_desc: Ash in full sprint leaping between fence tops at night, fog blurred with speed, a dark window ahead
lines: Over the fences, under the gate, up the drainpipe I have used nine hundred times.
Faster than anything on four legs tonight.
Fast enough that something inside is still... busy.
The door: shut. A door has never once been an obstacle. It is, however, always an insult.
In through the workroom window.
The threads on the walls — cut. All of them. Hanging like torn hems.
Something is standing in the parlor doorway, wearing the room.
The parlor. The kettle, screaming on the stove.
Elspeth in her chair. The light gone out of her hands.
I took the kettle off the fire. One paw. It took three tries.
Nobody will ever know.
The thread at my chest — the one that was always hers — cut.
Not quite.
One strand left. Thin as spite. Running out under the window, into the city.
Then that is where we are going.

hollow_court_first: A desk. A lamp. A queue of one.
'Name?' — I am a cat. — '...Vane's familiar. Nine allotted, one spent.'
'First visit is complimentary. Do try to make the others interesting.'
The stamp comes down. It is, I notice, a paw print. Neither of us remarks on this.
hollow_court_repeat: The desk again. The lamp again. The Clerk does not look up.
'Back so soon. The form remembers you, which saves us both time.'
The Toll is taken. Professionally. Almost gently.
The stairs up are longer than the fall down. They always are.
unpicked_won: It comes apart. Thread by thread. That was not supposed to happen.
Somewhere below the city, a clerk files something under 'irregular'.
